existingClaims.reason: The thermostat repair is conditional on scan-data diagnosis, while the existing THRGM-0002 card is unconditional, unscoped, and not confirmed across the article's engine applications by the current catalog pass.

reviewedSourceEvidence.howToFix: Verify actual coolant temperature with a scan tool vs. the gauge to separate a bad ECT sensor from a bad thermostat. If the engine won't reach ~195-210°F, replace the thermostat (and housing/gasket, commonly sold as an assembly) with an OEM-spec unit and refill/bleed the cooling system. Replace the ECT sensor if data shows an implausible reading.

reviewedSourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the water pump (ACDelco Professional water pump for the applicable V8) with a new gasket, and refill with GM DEXCOOL. Catch the weep-hole leak early to avoid an overheating event and possible head-gasket damage.
